# Unit test for function common
def test_common():
    # Basic case with common elements
    assert common([1, 2, 3], [2, 3, 4]) == [2, 3]
    
    # No common elements
    assert common([1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]) == []
    
    # Empty lists
    assert common([], [1, 2, 3]) == []
    assert common([1, 2, 3], []) == []
    assert common([], []) == []
    
    # Duplicates in inputs should be deduplicated in output
    assert common([1, 1, 2, 2, 3], [2, 3, 3, 4]) == [2, 3]
    
    # Identical lists
    assert common([5, 3, 1], [5, 3, 1]) == [1, 3, 5]
    
    # Result should be sorted even if inputs are unsorted
    assert common([9, 7, 5], [5, 7, 9]) == [5, 7, 9]
    assert common([3, 1, 2], [2, 3, 1]) == [1, 2, 3]
    
    # Single common element
    assert common([1, 2, 3], [3]) == [3]
    assert common([3], [1, 2, 3]) == [3]
    
    # String elements
    assert common(["apple", "banana", "cherry"], ["banana", "cherry", "date"]) == ["banana", "cherry"]
    
    # Mixed types that are comparable
    assert common([1, "a", 2.0], [2.0, "a"]) == [2.0, "a"]
    
    # Negative numbers
    assert common([-1, -2, 0], [0, -1, 5]) == [-1, 0]
    
    # One element contained multiple times in both
    assert common([7, 7, 7], [7, 7]) == [7]
    
    # Lists of different lengths
    assert common([1, 2], [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]) == [1, 2]
    
    # Result is a list type
    assert isinstance(common([1], [1]), list)
    
    # Boolean and int equality (True == 1 in Python)
    assert common([True, 2], [1, 2]) == [1, 2]
    
    print("All tests passed!")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_common()

# Unit test for function common
def test_common():
    # Basic case with common elements
    assert common([1, 2, 3, 4], [3, 4, 5, 6]) == [3, 4]

    # No common elements
    assert common([1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]) == []

    # Duplicates in both lists should still return unique results
    assert common([1, 1, 2, 2, 3], [2, 2, 3, 3]) == [2, 3]

    # Empty lists
    assert common([], []) == []
    assert common([1, 2, 3], []) == []
    assert common([], [1, 2, 3]) == []

    # One list is a subset of the other
    assert common([1, 2, 3], [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]) == [1, 2, 3]

    # Unsorted inputs should produce sorted output
    assert common([5, 3, 1], [1, 5, 9]) == [1, 5]

    # Works with strings
    assert common(["apple", "banana", "cherry"], ["banana", "date"]) == ["banana"]

    # Works with negative numbers and mixed values
    assert common([-1, 0, 5], [0, -1, 10]) == [-1, 0]

    # Single element lists
    assert common([7], [7]) == [7]
    assert common([7], [8]) == []

    # Common elements appear only once in result even if repeated many times
    assert common([1, 1, 1, 1], [1, 1]) == [1]

    # Works with floats
    assert common([1.5, 2.5, 3.5], [2.5, 3.5, 4.5]) == [2.5, 3.5]

    # Result is always sorted regardless of input order
    assert common([9, 4, 7], [7, 9, 4]) == [4, 7, 9]

    print("All tests passed!")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_common()
